solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Second application for computer device

parts.note: a mo is a brief moment, a second
to apply something is to put it to use

explanation.surface: Someone tries a gadget for the second time at the office desk.
explanation.definitionFit: The hand-held pointer that moves a cursor on screen is a standard computer peripheral.

clue.text: High aim to surround government with wise men

indicators.note: to surround means the jumbled letters enclose the government letter
high in its sense of intoxicated, so the letters of aim reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Lofty ambition to encircle the government with sages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like a description of the aim but, meaning drunk, it scrambles AIM into MAI; 'to surround' puts G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi are the three wise men of the Nativity story.

clue.text: During rebellion, upcoming artist and revolutionary is taken by police

indicators.note: during means these letters come in the middle of the rebellion

parts.note: unrest is rebellion, public disturbance

indicators.note: in a down clue, upcoming means the artist and revolutionary words are written upwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
red is a byword for a revolutionary

explanation.surface: During riots, a rising artist and a radical are arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' turns RA plus RED into DERAR, and 'During' puts it inside UNREST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held in custody after being detained is in the hands of the police.

clue.text: Quantity of old camping gear

parts.note: ex means former, old
a tent is camping equipment

explanation.surface: Someone asks how much of their old camping kit there is.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent is size or amount, how much of something there is.

clue.text: Working model's almost perfect, restricted by design

indicators.note: restricted means the shortened perfect is hemmed in between the two other pieces

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
to model is to pose; the 's is read as 'is'

indicators.note: almost means the word for perfect stops one letter short

parts.note: pure can mean perfect, flawless

explanation.surface: A catwalk model working hard seems nearly flawless, yet held back by the designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims PURE to PUR, and 'restricted' sets it between ON and POSE. 'by' belongs with 'design' in the definition, not to the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by design means doing it deliberately, intentionally, not by accident.

clue.text: Review to now include women's groups in a different way

indicators.note: review is read as re-view, looking back, so the word to is reversed
include means the women's groups go inside the word for now

parts.note: here can mean now, at this point
WIs are Women's Institutes, British women's community groups

explanation.surface: A call to review policy so it now includes women's groups.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute (WI) is a British women's organisation; 'include' puts WIS inside HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means differently, in some other manner.

clue.text: Put out summit broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is heard as spoken over the airwaves

parts.note: a peak is a summit

explanation.surface: A summit meeting is broadcast live.
explanation.definitionFit: To pique someone is to annoy or offend them, to put them out.

clue.text: Continue to study student's last essay which can't be edited

parts.note: to read on is to carry on studying
L is a learner, a student driver

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of essay

explanation.surface: A student reads on to the end of an essay that is locked.
explanation.definitionFit: A file marked so it can be viewed but not altered is a standard computing status.

clue.text: With zero exercise get plump

parts.note: O resembles zero
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: Without any exercise you get fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plump' is the verb, as in plump for, to choose.
explanation.definitionFit: To plump for something is to choose it, to make a choice.

clue.text: Recklessly I steam into making a guess

indicators.note: recklessly signals the letters charging about out of order

explanation.surface: Someone charges in carelessly, guessing as they go.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimation is a rough judgement, the act of guessing at a figure.

clue.text: Share costs on condition daughter moves in with child

indicators.note: moves in means the daughter's letter is placed inside the word for the condition

parts.note: gout is a medical condition of the joints

explanation.surface: A family splits the bills on condition that the daughter moves in with her baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves in' puts D inside GOUT to give GODUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To go Dutch is the idiom for each person paying their own share of a bill.

clue.text: Band has a couple of pints then starts off set

parts.note: a quart is two pints

indicators.note: starts off means the opening letter of the word set is removed

explanation.surface: A band has two pints at the bar before kicking off its set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts off' drops the S of 'set', leaving ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of four musicians playing together is a kind of band.

clue.text: Behave typically and nurture stray cat with efforts heartily welcomed

indicators.note: stray signals that the letters of nurture wander out of order
welcomed means the central letters are taken inside the word for the cat

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: heartily asks for the heart, the central letters, of efforts

explanation.surface: Someone raises a stray cat, and their efforts are warmly received.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of NURTURE gives RUNTRUE; 'heartily' takes FOR from the middle of eFFORts, and 'welcomed' puts it inside TOM.
explanation.definitionFit: To act exactly as expected, in character, is the idiom described here.

clue.text: Directing canoe child's play in light sea wind

indicators.note: directing a canoe steers it around, so its letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: a breeze is something easy, child's play

explanation.surface: Steering a canoe is easy in a light wind off the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle wind blowing in off the water is what a coastal breeze is.

clue.text: Pork belly starter with egg on side is ultimate fast food

parts.note: ham is pork meat

indicators.note: starter asks for the first letter of belly

parts.note: to egg on is to urge
R for right, a side

indicators.note: ultimate asks for the last letter of is

explanation.surface: A menu: pork belly to start, with egg on the side, the ultimate quick meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgers in buns are the classic takeaway meal of quick-service restaurants.

clue.text: Care about getting some land

indicators.note: about signals the letters of care being turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone worries about acquiring a plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of area, so it names a measured piece of ground.

clue.text: Without money for home, therefore allowed to borrow against investing

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
so means therefore

indicators.note: investing in its old sense of clothing or surrounding: the lending word wraps the letter for against

parts.note: lent means given on loan, allowed to borrow
V for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A homeowner with no cash is allowed to borrow against an investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' is used in its sense of enclosing: LENT goes round V to give LVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bankrupt person or firm has no money to pay its debts.

clue.text: Took legal action over disgrace suffered

indicators.note: over means the legal word goes over, covering, the disgrace word

parts.note: sued means took legal action
a stain is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: Someone went to court over a disgrace they had suffered.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain an injury or loss is to suffer it.

clue.text: Both endlessly move round and stay away from hard battle

indicators.note: both endlessly means each of the two words loses its last letter

parts.note: to skirt is to move round the edge of something
to miss something is to stay away from it
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Both armies keep circling and avoiding a tough battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both endlessly' cuts SKIRT to SKIR and MISS to MIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirmish is a small, brief fight, a minor battle.

clue.text: Excellent book looks back describing family missing Italy

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing round: the reversed looking words go around the shortened family
back means the looking words are read in reverse

parts.note: the plural looks is taken as two lots of see, to look

indicators.note: missing means the letter for Italy is dropped from the family word

parts.note: kin means family
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A wonderful book looks back on a family that has left Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's 'looks' does double duty as SEE twice: each reversed gives EES, and 'describing' wraps them round KN (KIN with I removed). BEES KNEES is old slang praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something the bee's knees is a jokey idiom meaning it is the very best.

clue.text: A fan of Not Going Out after third episode

indicators.note: after means the scrambled letters come behind the picked letter
third asks for the third letter of the word episode
Going Out, the sitcom title, is read as letters going out of place

explanation.surface: A devotee of the sitcom Not Going Out catches up after the third episode.
explanation.walkthrough: Not Going Out is a British TV sitcom; the title splits into fodder 'Not' and its anagram signal 'Going Out', giving NTO after the I of epIsode.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is informal for being keen on it, an enthusiast.

clue.text: Happy over half caught in jail break

indicators.note: caught in means the half word is trapped inside the rearranged jail letters
break signals the letters of jail broken up and rearranged
half asks for the first two letters of over

explanation.surface: A prisoner is cheerful about a jailbreak, half caught already.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges JAIL into JIAL, and 'caught in' puts OV inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Jovial means cheerful and good-humoured, in high spirits.

clue.text: Pay back kindness of clergyman framing fine art nouveau work

indicators.note: framing means the clergyman's letters sit on either side of the rest

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

indicators.note: work signals the letters being worked into a new shape

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A vicar frames a fine Art Nouveau piece as thanks for a kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges F plus ART NOUVEAU into ETURNAFAVOU, and 'framing' puts it between the two Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: To repay a good turn done to you is the idiom here.

clue.text: Series right to the end causes outrage

indicators.note: to the end means the letter for right moves to the end of the series word

parts.note: a range is a series, as in a product range

explanation.surface: A TV series moving to the right causes uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is strong indignation, the feeling of outrage.

clue.text: Queen admits yen to have new anthem

indicators.note: admits means the queen's letters let the yen letter inside

parts.note: HM is Her Majesty, the Queen
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: The Queen lets in a longing to have a new national song.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a song of praise, often a religious one sung in church.

clue.text: Frustrating online game cut short by wifi connection failing finally

parts.note: E, as in e-mail, stands for electronic or online

indicators.note: cut short means the game's last letter is chopped off

parts.note: ludo is a board game

indicators.note: finally asks for the end letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: An online game is cut off by a dropped wifi connection, frustratingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes LUDO down to LUD; 'finally' takes I, N and G from the ends of wifi, connection and failing.
explanation.definitionFit: Eluding someone, escaping their grasp, frustrates their efforts to catch you.

clue.text: College informally has some continuing in retirement

indicators.note: in a down clue, in retirement means the taken letters go back, reading upwards
some means a few letters are taken from inside the word continuing

explanation.surface: A college keeps some retired staff on.
explanation.definitionFit: Uni is the casual short form of university, a place of higher education.

clue.text: No housing check on island shows lack of experience

indicators.note: housing means the word for no contains the other pieces

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

indicators.note: on means the checking word sits next to, upon, the island letter

parts.note: to vet is to check

explanation.surface: Refusing to put up a security check on an island shows a green official.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocence, the simple trust of someone without worldly experience.

clue.text: Moved snake-like and cut east penetrating group of animals

parts.note: to slit is to cut

indicators.note: penetrating means the letter for east gets inside the word for the animal group

parts.note: a herd is a group of animals such as cattle
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A snake slid off, cutting east through a herd of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penetrating' puts E inside HERD to give HERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Slithering is the sliding, twisting motion of a snake.

clue.text: Delay arising when not tellin' the truth in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means the word is judged by how it is spoken out loud

parts.note: someone not telling the truth is lyin', dropped g and all

explanation.surface: A liar holds things up when giving evidence at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped g of 'tellin'' signals the dropped g of lyin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is a morning spent in bed later than usual, putting off getting up.
